original_value: A new microwave sensor is proposed to characterize the complex relative permittivity of building non-magnetic materials and used in the characterization of three concrete samples. The proposed sensor structure consists of a log-periodic planar antenna with microstrip elements tilted forward by an angle β and printed, alternately, on the top and bottom sides of a dielectric layer. The operation principle is based on the measurement of the scattering parameters S11 and S21 in a free space propagation transmitter-receiver setup, for both cases with the material under test (MUT) sample (non-line-of-sight, NLOS) and without it (line-of-sight, LOS). A prototype is fabricated and measured to determine the scattering parameters of concrete samples. After measurements, the obtained results are used in the efficient and accurate Nicolson–Ross–Weir (NRW) method, making it possible to estimate the values of the complex relative permittivity of the concrete blocks. The sensor design is demonstrated from initial simulations to measurements for validation of the developed prototype. The obtained results for the complex relative permittivity of concrete are in agreement with those available in the literature and the difference between the simulated and measurement results for the sensor antenna resonant frequency is 4.71%. The used measurement setup can be applied to characterize different types of solid or liquid dielectric materials.

result.paraphrase: A new microwave sensor is proposed for characterizing the complex relative permittivity of non-magnetic building materials and is applied to three concrete samples. Its structure uses a log-periodic planar antenna with microstrip elements tilted forward by angle β and printed alternately on the top and bottom sides of a dielectric layer. The operating principle relies on measuring the scattering parameters S11 and S21 in a free-space transmitter-receiver setup, both with the material-under-test sample present in a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) configuration and without it in a line-of-sight (LOS) case. A prototype is built and measured to obtain the scattering parameters of the concrete samples. The measured results are then used with the efficient and accurate Nicolson–Ross–Weir (NRW) method to estimate the complex relative permittivity of the concrete blocks. The sensor is validated from initial simulations through measurements of the developed prototype. The resulting complex relative permittivity values for concrete agree with those reported in the literature, and the difference between simulated and measured sensor antenna resonant frequencies is 4.71%. This measurement setup can also be used to characterize various solid or liquid dielectric materials.
